Let me view reference images one at a time, starting with my top candidates.
Anthracnose shows large shiny black lesions and reddish discoloration, quite different from the discrete brown spots in the test image. Let me check Physoderma_Brown_Spot.

Physoderma Brown Spot on stem shows dark purplish-black spots on a green stalk. The spot pattern is somewhat similar but the stalk is green vs. the dry mature stalk in the test image. Let me check more candidates.
Diplodia stalk rot shows a dry bent stalk but without the distinct spots visible in the test image. Let me check Purple_Leaf_Sheath.

Purple Leaf Sheath shows dark brown/purple lesions on a green stalk with distinct bordered spots. The spot shapes are somewhat similar to the test image but again on green tissue. Let me check Physoderma_Stalk_Rot and Charcoal_Stalk_Rot.
Physoderma Stalk Rot shows dense dark spots near nodes on green tissue. Let me check Charcoal_Stalk_Rot.
Charcoal stalk rot shows internal shredding with sclerotia, very different from the external spots in the test image. Let me check Stewart's Disease on stem and one more reference.
This Diplodia stalk rot reference is a much closer match. Both show a dry tan stalk with small dark brown spots/pycnidia on the rind near the node. Let me use my last view.

Bacterial stalk rot shows water-soaked mushy tissue, not a match.

**Analysis summary:**

The test image shows a dry, tan-colored mature corn stalk with discrete small dark brown spots/structures on the rind surface, concentrated near the node. Comparing across all 8 references:

- **Diplodia_Stalk_Rot (Corn_Disease_20.jpg)** is the closest visual match: same dry tan stalk, same small dark spots (pycnidia) embedded in the rind near the node, same overall appearance.
- Anthracnose: large shiny black lesions, not matching
- Physoderma Brown Spot/Stalk Rot: spots on green tissue, different pattern
- Purple Leaf Sheath: larger irregular lesions on green tissue
- Charcoal Stalk Rot: internal shredding with sclerotia
- Bacterial Stalk Rot: water-soaked mushy tissue

The KB confirms: Diplodia stalk rot shows "small black structures embedded within the lower stalk rind."
